production.note: US model years. Sports Car Market (Josh Jacquot): the second generation arrived for the 1988 model year and ran through 1991, with the Si trim offered for the whole run.

body.note: Two-seat Kammback sport coupe with a rear liftback, sold as its own model alongside the Civic.

displacementL.note: 1,590 cc ('more displacement (1,590 cc versus 1,493 cc)' for the Si against the base car). Hagerty's spec box agrees: 'inline-4, 1590 cc' (hagerty-crx-si).

aspiration.note: Inferred: no opened source mentions any forced induction on the Si's 1.6-litre four.

drivetrain.note: Inferred: front-engine, front-wheel-drive Civic-based platform as described by the cited pages.

transmission.note: The HF and Si came 'exclusively with a 5-speed manual gearbox'; only the base CRX offered an automatic. Hagerty's spec box: 'Transmission: 5-speed manual'.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL source class for power (no Honda page; not a major-magazine panel). 1988 rating. Quote (Sports Car Market, Josh Jacquot): the Si engine was 'producing 105 hp in 1988 and 108 hp from 1989 to '91'. Motor Authority (Sean Szymkowski): the 1.6 'breathed 105 horsepower into the CRX Si' (ma-crx-si); Hagerty's spec box for the 1989 model also prints '105 hp @ 6000 rpm' (hagerty-crx-si). The rating later rose to 108 hp; the sources disagree on when (SCM says from 1989, but Hagerty's 1989 box still shows 105 hp, which matches the usual 1990 facelift), so the launch-year 105 hp rating is used.

weightLb.note: 1988 Si, 5-speed manual. Quote (Sports Car Market, Josh Jacquot): 'Weighing a mere 2,017 pounds, the 1988 CRX Si was a featherweight'. Motor Authority (Sean Szymkowski) agrees: the 1988 Si 'tipped the scales at 2,017 pounds' (ma-crx-si): two independent editorial outlets with named authors. See discrepancies for Hagerty's 1989 figure.

sources.title: 1988 Honda CRX Si: 100 Cars That Matter (Sean Szymkowski, 9 July 2019)
2020 Hagerty Bull Market selection: 1988-91 Honda CRX Si

discrepancies.reason: Hagerty's spec box for the 1989 CRX Si prints a rounded 'Weight: 2100 lb'; Sports Car Market and Motor Authority both give 2,017 lb for the 1988 car. Different model year and evident rounding.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 2,017 lb: two named-author outlets agree on it for the 1988 reference year; Hagerty's 2,100 lb is a rounded figure for the 1989 model.

discrepancies.reason: Sources disagree on when the rating rose from 105 to 108 hp: Sports Car Market says 'producing 105 hp in 1988 and 108 hp from 1989 to '91', while Hagerty's 1989 spec box still prints '105 hp @ 6000 rpm'.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 105 hp, the undisputed 1988 launch rating; 1988 is the record's reference year either way.

provisionalNote: Power (105 hp) rests on Sports Car Market, Motor Authority and Hagerty agreeing, none of them a manufacturer page or a major-magazine specification panel as the power rule requires; no Honda page was opened, and the sources disagree on when the rating rose to 108 hp (see discrepancies). Weight (2,017 lb) meets weight step 2 (two independent named-author outlets agreeing). A Honda press or brochure page, or a major-magazine specification panel, would make the record normal.
